guarantees.claim: On negation of rst_ni (reset), rx_val_q is asynchronously set to 16'h0.
When rst_ni is high and tick_baud_x16 is asserted, rx_val_q is synchronously updated to the shifted value {rx_val_q[14:0], rx_in}.
When tick_baud_x16 is deasserted and rst_ni remains high, rx_val_q retains its previous value.

assumptions.claim: tick_baud_x16 must be a single-cycle pulse to prevent multiple shifts within one baud period.
assumptions.cond: when tick_baud_x16 is used to qualify shifting
assumptions.risk: If tick_baud_x16 stays high for multiple cycles, rx_val_q shifts multiple times, corrupting the sample buffer used for bit detection.

assumptions.claim: rx_in must be stable and valid during the cycle when tick_baud_x16 is asserted.
assumptions.risk: A glitch or transition on rx_in during sampling would capture an incorrect bit into rx_val_q, potentially causing framing or data corruption.

uncertain_points.claim: rx_val_q is hardcoded to 16 bits, implying a fixed 16x oversampling ratio. If the UART configuration parameterizes the oversampling rate, this chunk would silently mismatch.
uncertain_points.risk: Mismatch between shift register depth and actual oversampling count could lead to incorrect bit sampling or corrupted data reception.
